binding.compilerLocation: Linux target executing RCL compiler RBC

proposal.diagnosis: Euclidean reduction requires the remainder of a divided by b. The reversed remainder can cycle and divides by zero when a is zero and b is nonzero. The corrected reduction preserves the nonnegative base result for signed inputs and zero boundaries.
The recurrence skips the immediately preceding second value. Using n minus two restores the sum of the previous two values while preserving F(0)=0 and F(1)=1.
The recurrence adds twice n instead of its square. Multiply n by itself; the existing nonpositive base case remains zero.
